instrument: Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI-22; ZBI-12; ZBI-4 screen)
developer_owner: S.H. Zarit; Mapi Research Trust is the exclusive licensor, distributor and translator, including electronic versions
population: Family/informal caregivers (developed for dementia; widely used in ALS, stroke and SCI caregivers)
construct: Subjective caregiver burden
scoring: 0-4 Likert per item; total 0-88 (ZBI-22)
validation_refs: Zarit, Reever & Bach-Peterson 1980 Gerontologist 20:649 doi:10.1093/geront/20.6.649 [PK]; Bedard et al. 2001 Gerontologist 41:652 doi:10.1093/geront/41.5.652 [PK]
license_type: Copyrighted; licensed via Mapi/ePROVIDE
commercial_permission: Commercial licence required through ePROVIDE. No public fee schedule. Secondary sources say it is free for clinicians and non-funded academic research only
electronic_admin_notes: Mapi controls the electronic versions, so expect an e-version licence and a migration/screenshot review. The ePROVIDE page redirected to a maintenance notice when accessed
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: the standard caregiver-burden comparator in ALS caregiver studies [PK]
evidence_label: V (licensor role, via Mapi news page excerpt); PK (refs)

developer_owner: Novak & Guest (article (c) Gerontological Society of America)
construct: Multidimensional burden: time-dependence, developmental, physical, social, emotional
scoring: 0-4 per item; total 0-96; subscale sums
validation_refs: Novak & Guest 1989 Gerontologist 29(6):798-803 doi:10.1093/geront/29.6.798 [PK]
license_type: Published in journal article; no licensor found [UNR]
commercial_permission: Unknown. Ask the authors and the publisher (OUP/GSA) [UNR]
electronic_admin_notes: No published e-version terms
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium-high: its time-dependence subscale captures assistance demand; used in ALS caregiver research [PK]
evidence_label: UNR (licence); V (article and copyright notice); PK

developer_owner: C.W. Given, B. Given et al. (Michigan State University); article published by Wiley
population: Family caregivers of people with physical impairment, Alzheimer's disease or cancer
construct: Caregiver reactions: esteem, schedule, finances, family support, health
scoring: 1-5 Likert; mean per subscale
validation_refs: Given et al. 1992 Res Nurs Health 15:271-283 doi:10.1002/nur.4770150406 [PK]
license_type: No licensor found [UNR]
electronic_admin_notes: No published e-version terms
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: includes positive aspects (esteem), useful for AT/BCI care-partner outcomes

instrument: PROMIS (Physical Function, Fatigue, Ability to Participate in Social Roles & Activities; item banks, short forms, CAT)
developer_owner: PROMIS Health Organization; distributed by HealthMeasures (Northwestern University)
population: Adults (general and chronic disease); calibrated in US general-population samples
construct: Self-reported physical function, fatigue, social participation and other domains
items: Item banks (PF and Fatigue banks are large, about 95-165 items [PK]); short forms 4-20 items; CAT typically 4-12 items
scoring: IRT T-score (mean 50, SD 10 in US reference population); HealthMeasures Scoring Service is free
validation_refs: Cella et al. 2010 J Clin Epidemiol 63:1179 doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2010.04.011 [PK]; Rose et al. 2014 J Clin Epidemiol (PF) [PK]; Terwee et al. 2021 Qual Life Res 30:2729 (MIC) doi:10.1007/s11136-021-02925-y [V]
license_type: Copyrighted; free for individual research/clinical use; commercial users must seek permission
commercial_permission: Required. Commercial = any non-tax-exempt or for-profit entity (NeuroMetric qualifies). Integration into proprietary systems (apps, CATs, web portals) needs written approval. Wording/layout may not be modified
electronic_admin_notes: Digital-administration screenshot review: $750 per standard English measure (commercial, study duration or 3-year term); custom form $900; Assessment Center API Single Institution $6,000/yr; Distributor $18,000/yr; custom T-score table $1,500 per measure; translations $1,100 per language per measure. A CAT engine using PROMIS calibrations needs API licence or written permission
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for SCI and stroke (PROMIS-based SCI-QOL and Neuro-QoL exist); moderate for ALS (floor effects in advanced ALS likely [INF])
evidence_label: V (HealthMeasures fees page and Measure Library terms; PROMIS T&C PDF v2014)

instrument: Neuro-QoL (incl. Upper Extremity Function/Fine Motor-ADL, Fatigue, Communication, Ability to Participate, Stigma)
developer_owner: NINDS-funded; distributed by HealthMeasures (Northwestern)
population: Adults and children with neurological conditions (development samples included ALS, stroke, MS, PD, epilepsy [PK])
construct: HRQoL in neurology: physical, mental and social domains
items: Item banks plus short forms (typically 8-item SF); CAT
scoring: IRT T-scores (some referenced to a clinical sample)
validation_refs: Cella et al. 2012 Neurology 78:1860 doi:10.1212/WNL.0b013e318258f744 [PK]
license_type: Same HealthMeasures terms as PROMIS
electronic_admin_notes: Same as PROMIS: screenshot review fees and API licence
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: ALS and stroke were in the development populations [PK]. The Upper Extremity and Communication banks are directly relevant to digital-access outcomes

developer_owner: Tulsky et al. (Kessler Foundation / University of Delaware); distributed via Assessment Center and REDCap
construct: Physical/medical, emotional and social HRQoL; SCI-specific banks (e.g., Independence, Bladder, Bowel, Pressure Ulcers)
items: Multiple item banks with CAT and short forms
scoring: IRT T-scores
validation_refs: Tulsky et al. 2015 J Spinal Cord Med 38(3) (system overview, CC BY) [PK]
license_type: Listed as free (non-commercial); commercial terms not published [UNR]
electronic_admin_notes: Free electronic versions in Assessment Center/REDCap. CAT administration app $500/yr for up to 10 iPads (per SRAlab page)
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for SCI

developer_owner: C. Jenkinson & R. Fitzpatrick, University of Oxford; licensed by Oxford University Innovation (OUI)
construct: Disease-specific HRQoL: physical mobility (10), ADL/independence (10), eating and drinking (3), communication (7), emotional reactions (10)
scoring: 5-point items over the past 2 weeks; domain scores 0-100 (0 = best)
validation_refs: Jenkinson et al. 1999 J Neurol 246(Suppl 3):III16 [PK]; Jenkinson et al. 2007 ALSAQ-5 vs ALSAQ-40 longitudinal [PK]; CADTH edaravone review notes limited construct validity for communication/ADL domains https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK542356/
license_type: Copyrighted; licence via OUI 'Request a licence'
commercial_permission: Licence required. Terms and fees not public
electronic_admin_notes: OUI lists ePRO/eCOA as an administration mode. Expect an OUI e-version licence
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for ALS
evidence_label: V (OUI page: owner, licensing route, ePRO mode)

developer_owner: Cedarbaum et al. (BDNF ALS Study Group); rights holder not confirmed [UNR]. A self-administered version is listed for licensing by Columbia Technology Ventures (CU25205)
construct: ALS functional status: bulbar, fine motor, gross motor, respiratory
respondent: ClinRO (rater interview); self-report and online versions exist (PRO)
scoring: 0-4 per item; total 0-48 (higher = better)
validation_refs: Cedarbaum et al. 1999 J Neurol Sci 169:13 doi:10.1016/S0022-510X(99)00210-5 [PK]; Bakker et al. 2020 JNNP self-administration (BMJ) [V-search]; ALSFRS-R Summit call to action (CC BY-NC-ND) [V-search]
license_type: Not determined [UNR]; widely reproduced
commercial_permission: Unknown. The Columbia self-administered version is offered for licence
electronic_admin_notes: Trial raters must be NEALS (or ENCALS) certified, e.g. the HEALEY platform protocol. Self-administered versions differ subtly from each other
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Very high for ALS: regulatory-grade primary endpoint. Floor effects in late-stage/locked-in users
evidence_label: UNR (rights); V (training requirement via protocol excerpt; Columbia listing)

developer_owner: Fournier et al. (Emory)
construct: Overall disability (Rasch-built)
scoring: Rasch-normed total [PK]
validation_refs: Fournier et al. 2020 JAMA Neurol 77(4):480 doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2019.4490 [PK]
license_type: Stated to be publicly available at no charge (per JAMA abstract excerpt)
electronic_admin_notes: None published
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for ALS: a patient-reported alternative to ALSFRS-R
evidence_label: V (search excerpt of JAMA abstract); PK

developer_owner: World Health Organization (WHOQOL Group); national WHOQOL centres
construct: QoL: physical, psychological, social relationships, environment, plus 2 general items
scoring: 1-5 items; domain scores transformed to 4-20 and 0-100
validation_refs: WHOQOL Group 1998 Psychol Med 28:551 [PK]; Skevington et al. 2004 Qual Life Res 13:299 [PK]
license_type: Copyright WHO; permission via WHO permissions form / national centre
commercial_permission: Required. WHO says permission is required for commercial uses. NZ centre charges NZ$500 per commercially funded study (NZ only)
electronic_admin_notes: No published e-version rules; treat as faithful-reproduction only [INF]
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: generic QoL. Used as intake measure in SRAlab NCT07407725
evidence_label: V (WHO permissions page; NZ centre terms); PK (refs)

developer_owner: EuroQol Research Foundation
construct: Health status (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression) + EQ VAS
scoring: 5 levels per dimension; index via country value sets; VAS 0-100
validation_refs: Herdman et al. 2011 Qual Life Res 20:1727 doi:10.1007/s11136-011-9903-x [PK]
license_type: Copyrighted; registration required for all users
commercial_permission: Commercial licence fee set by the EuroQol office from registration details. Digital formats have a separate commercial fee structure (2022 notice)
electronic_admin_notes: Must use EuroQol-supplied/approved digital versions or obtain approval for implementation [PK]
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: needed for HTA/utility. The 'walking about' wording is a known problem for wheelchair users in SCI/ALS [PK]
evidence_label: V (SRAlab cost text); AE (secondary descriptions of digital fee change)

instrument: PIADS (Psychosocial Impact of Assistive Devices Scale)
developer_owner: J. Jutai & H. Day (copyright holders [PK])
construct: Perceived psychosocial impact: competence (12), adaptability (6), self-esteem (8)
scoring: -3 to +3 per item; subscale means
validation_refs: Jutai & Day 2002 Technol Disabil 14:107 [PK]; Tofani et al. psychometric systematic review (CIRRIS) [V-search]
license_type: Listed as free (SRAlab); author permission is customary [PK]
electronic_admin_notes: No published e-version rules
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: AT/BCI-specific impact. Used as a PRO in SRAlab NCT07407725

developer_owner: L. Demers, R. Weiss-Lambrou, B. Ska
construct: Satisfaction with AT device (8) and services (4)
scoring: 1-5 satisfaction per item; device, services and total mean scores; choose 3 most important items
validation_refs: Demers et al. 1996 Assist Technol 8(1):3 [V via SRAlab]; Demers et al. 2002 Technol Disabil 14:101 [PK]
license_type: SRAlab lists it as free; manual historically distributed by IMPT [PK]
electronic_admin_notes: None published
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: AT satisfaction

developer_owner: M.J. Scherer, Institute for Matching Person & Technology (Webster NY)
construct: Predisposition to use AT; person-technology match
scoring: Item ratings; computerized scoring/interpretation offered by IMPT
validation_refs: Scherer & colleagues (multiple) [PK]
license_type: Listed as free (SRAlab) with order form at MatchingPersonandTechnology.com; IMPT sells some materials
electronic_admin_notes: IMPT provides electronic forms on its own site
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: AT selection rather than outcome

instrument: FMA (Functional Mobility Assessment) / FEW (Functioning Everyday with a Wheelchair; FEW-C)
developer_owner: University of Pittsburgh (Mills, Holm, Schmeler et al.)
construct: Satisfaction with mobility-device-related function
scoring: 6-point agreement scale per item [PK]
validation_refs: Mills et al. 2002 FEW development [PK]; FEW v2.0 ICC(3,k)=.86 [V-search excerpt]
license_type: FMA: paper free for non-commercial use; commercial licence from Pitt. FEW: [UNR]
commercial_permission: FMA commercial: $10,000 per commercial study ($5,000 if sponsor has 50 or fewer employees and 100 or fewer participants); annual use licence $5,000 (fewer than 1,001 uses) to $20,000 (more than 10,000 uses); 'not negotiable'
electronic_admin_notes: Computerized versions on request from Pitt. Self-translations must be assigned to Pitt
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: wheelchair-mobility-centric; little coverage of computer access

developer_owner: Law, Baptiste, Carswell, McColl, Polatajko, Pollock; COPM Inc.
construct: Self-perceived occupational performance and satisfaction on client-identified problems
scoring: Performance and satisfaction 1-10; change of 2 or more points often cited as clinically important [PK]
validation_refs: Law et al. 1990 Can J Occup Ther 57:82 [PK]; Carswell et al. 2004 review [PK]
license_type: Copyrighted; purchased/subscription
commercial_permission: Licence/purchase required; integration into third-party software not addressed publicly [UNR]
electronic_admin_notes: COPM Inc. sells a web app and digital PDF. Third-party electronic implementation needs permission [INF]
cost_if_known: CAD 52.45 manual/form kit; CAD 225.45 DVD kit (2012 prices per SRAlab)
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: individualized goals. A modified COPM is used in SRAlab NCT07407725

developer_owner: Kiresuk & Sherman (method); Turner-Stokes (rehab adaptation)
construct: Attainment of individually set goals
scoring: Each goal -2..+2 (baseline usually -1 or -2); T = 50 + 10*sum(w_i*x_i)/sqrt((1-rho)*sum(w_i^2) + rho*(sum w_i)^2), rho = 0.3
validation_refs: Kiresuk & Sherman 1968 Community Ment Health J 4:443 [PK]; Turner-Stokes 2009 Clin Rehabil 23:362 [PK]
license_type: Method; free
commercial_permission: No licence needed for the method. Do not copy proprietary GAS-light forms verbatim [INF]
electronic_admin_notes: Easy to implement; needs a goal-setting workflow with clinician
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: individualizes digital-access goals across ALS/SCI/stroke

developer_owner: NASA Ames (Hart & Staveland)
construct: Subjective workload: mental, physical and temporal demand, performance, effort, frustration
scoring: 0-100 per subscale (21 gradations); weighted or raw (RTLX) mean
validation_refs: Hart & Staveland 1988 Adv Psychol 52:139 [PK]; Hart 2006 HFES 50:904 [PK]
license_type: Free/open; NASA says no permission needed, including for modifications and translations
commercial_permission: Allowed (no NASA permission needed per NASA pages)
electronic_admin_notes: NASA offers a paper and iOS app. Free electronic implementation is allowed
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: workload of an input method. Used in SRAlab NCT07407725. Not a clinical PRO; the 'physical demand' item is ambiguous for paralysed users [INF]

developer_owner: J. Brooke (originally Digital Equipment Corp.)
construct: Perceived usability
scoring: 1-5; SUS = 2.5 * [sum(odd items - 1) + sum(5 - even items)], range 0-100
validation_refs: Brooke 1996 (Usability Evaluation in Industry) [PK]; Brooke 2013 J Usability Stud 8(2):29-40 [V-search]; Bangor et al. 2008 IJHCI [PK]
license_type: Free; acknowledgement of source requested
electronic_admin_notes: Free to implement electronically
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: device usability. Used in SRAlab NCT07407725
evidence_label: AE (secondary quotes of Brooke's condition of use); PK

developer_owner: L. Krupp et al. (copyright Dr Krupp per secondary sources)
population: MS, SLE; widely used in ALS, SCI, stroke
construct: Fatigue severity and impact on functioning
scoring: 1-7 per item; mean score; 4 or more commonly indicates fatigue
validation_refs: Krupp et al. 1989 Arch Neurol 46:1121 [PK]
license_type: Free for non-profit research; permission required for pharmaceutical (commercial) studies (secondary sources)
electronic_admin_notes: None published
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High: fatigue limits BCI/eye-gaze session length in ALS/SCI

developer_owner: Whiteneck et al., Craig Hospital
construct: Participation (ICIDH handicap): physical independence, cognitive independence, mobility, occupation, social integration, economic self-sufficiency
scoring: Each dimension 0-100 (100 = no handicap); Physical Independence weights hours of paid and unpaid assistance per day [PK]
validation_refs: Whiteneck et al. 1992 Arch Phys Med Rehabil 73:519 [PK]
license_type: Free (SRAlab)
electronic_admin_notes: None published
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for SCI. The assistance-hours items are a validated way to measure caregiver time [PK]

developer_owner: Cardol et al. (Amsterdam UMC)
construct: Perceived participation and autonomy (indoors, outdoors, family role, social relations, work/education)
scoring: Domain scores (higher = more restriction) [PK]
validation_refs: Cardol et al. 1999 Clin Rehabil 13:411 [PK]
license_type: Not free / cost not known (SRAlab)
electronic_admin_notes: None published
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium

developer_owner: Catz & Itzkovich (Loewenstein Rehabilitation Center); standardized procedures (c) Jefferson Center for Outcomes and Measurement
construct: Independence in self-care, respiration and sphincter management, mobility
scoring: 0-100 (self-care 0-20; respiration/sphincter 0-40; mobility 0-40)
validation_refs: Catz et al. 1997 Spinal Cord 35:850 [PK]; Itzkovich et al. 2007 Disabil Rehabil 29:1926 [PK]; Catz et al. 2007 Spinal Cord 45:275 [PK]
license_type: Published in article; listed as free (SRAlab). The Jefferson procedures document says it may not be modified without permission
electronic_admin_notes: Do not modify wording. Electronic form must be faithful [INF]
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for SCI

developer_owner: UDSMR (Uniform Data System for Medical Rehabilitation)
construct: Burden of care / disability: 13 motor and 5 cognitive items
scoring: 1-7 per item; 18-126
validation_refs: Many; see UDSMR bibliography [PK]
license_type: Proprietary; licence required
commercial_permission: Licence from UDSMR; fees vary by use; research project tracking form
electronic_admin_notes: UDSMR licenses vendors that build FIM into products
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Historical: replaced by Section GG in IRF-PAI (Oct 2019, per secondary sources)

instrument: IRF-PAI Section GG (Self-Care GG0130, Mobility GG0170)
developer_owner: US CMS
population: Post-acute care (IRF, SNF, LTCH, home health)

items: About 7 self-care + 17 mobility items (per secondary source)
scoring: 6-level scale (06 independent ... 01 dependent) + activity-not-attempted codes

license_type: US federal government work (17 USC 105), so no copyright is expected [INF]
electronic_admin_notes: Follow CMS coding guidance/decision tree when implementing
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Medium: used as intake in SRAlab NCT07407725. Does not cover computer/communication access

instrument: ISNCSCI (International Standards for Neurological Classification of SCI)
developer_owner: ASIA / ISCoS
construct: Neurological level, AIS grade, motor/sensory scores
items: Worksheet (10 key muscles each side; 28 dermatomes light touch/pin prick each side)
scoring: Upper and lower extremity motor scores, sensory scores, NLI, AIS A-E (algorithmic)
validation_refs: Kirshblum et al. 2011 J Spinal Cord Med 34:535 [PK]; Rupp et al. 2021 Top Spinal Cord Inj Rehabil 27(2):1 [PK]
license_type: Worksheet CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (ASIA)
commercial_permission: Commercial use, derivatives or clinical-trial use need ASIA permission
electronic_admin_notes: Training (ASIA InSTeP) expected for examiners [PK]. Electronic worksheet would be a derivative, so permission is needed
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: High for SCI (stratification). Abbreviated ISNCSCI is used in SRAlab NCT07407725

instrument: ECAS (Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen)
developer_owner: S. Abrahams, University of Edinburgh
population: ALS (designed for motor-impaired respondents: oral or written answers)
construct: Cognition (ALS-specific: language, fluency, executive; non-specific: memory, visuospatial) + behaviour (carer interview)
scoring: Domain and total scores; education-adjusted cut-offs; alternate forms A/B/C; remote ECAS
validation_refs: Abrahams et al. 2014 ALS FTD 15:9 [PK]; ECAS A-B-C alternate forms (TCD) [V-search]
license_type: Copyright licence: free for non-commercial academic research and health purposes
commercial_permission: Commercial licence agreement required for any other purpose, including commercially sponsored trials (contact via ECAS site)
electronic_admin_notes: Remote ECAS available. Electronic implementation needs licence [INF]
relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Very high for ALS: cognitive status affects BCI use. Used in SRAlab NCT07407725

developer_owner: Z. Nasreddine; MoCA Cognition
construct: Global cognition screen
scoring: Total 0-30 (+1 for 12 or fewer years of education); 26 or more = normal (original cut-off)
validation_refs: Nasreddine et al. 2005 J Am Geriatr Soc 53:695 [PK]
license_type: Copyrighted. Free use for universities/clinics/health professionals; commercial entity/pharma needs prior written permission and licensing agreement
electronic_admin_notes: Training and certification mandatory since 1 Sep 2019. Now optional for screening/triage on total score, still required for interpreting subscores. MoCA's own digital tools; app about $10/month per rater (SRAlab)

relevance_ALS_SCI_stroke: Low-medium: drawing and writing items are not feasible with paralysed hands. Prefer ECAS for ALS

developer_owner: Shirley Ryan AbilityLab (PI A. Jayaraman); Neuralink Corp listed as collaborator
